detail.longDescription:
Hakone is a special place for Japanese people. Inspired by the history and memories of countless travelers who have passed through this transit hub located on the historic Tokaido Road running from Nihonbashi Bridge in Edo (Tokyo) to Sanjo Ohashi Bridge in Kyoto, Hakone Honbako has also established its presence as a good transit point for modern-day travelers on the Tokaido Road.

Playing an important role in the gastronomic scene of Hakone, the restaurant, Hakone Honbako, is a four-minute walk from Naka-Gora cable car station and can also be accessed by a 40-minute taxi ride from JR Odawara Station. Converted from a publication distributor’s recreational facility , Hakone Honbako is nicknamed “Book Auberge” as it has installed large bookshelves stretching from the floor to the two-story ceiling on two walls next to the gently rising stairs to pay tribute to its own history.

The restaurant has been helmed since 2023 by Chef Yukihiro Hagiwara, who honed his culinary skills at a restaurant of the Salone Group, headquartered in Yokohama, to run high-end Italian restaurants, and a one-star restaurant in Puglia, Italy, before he joined Hakone Honbako in 2021. He combines his proven culinary skills with local ingredients from Shizuoka and Kanagawa to create innovative dishes that pay tribute to Tokaido.
Sous Chef Aoi Nakano trained at a one-star restaurant in Puglia, Italy, and a three-star restaurant in Denmark, and then joined Hakone Honbako in 2021 and was promoted to Sous Chef in March 2023.

Hakone Honbako features natural ingredients, such as seafood from the long-established Sasue Maeda Fish Shop in Yaizu, Shizuoka, organic vegetables from Kitayama Farm in Fujinomiya, also in Shizuoka, and natural ingredients from Keita Tanida the Natural Ingredients Hunter. All these producers are sought after not only in Kanagawa and Shizuoka but all over Japan. In addition, the restaurant sources ingredients from local producers with whom it has forged close ties. These ingredients are transformed into creative dishes that pay tribute to the location and food culture of the region. For example, “Botamochizaka” is inspired by kuri-botamochi (rice balls covered with chestnut paste), the specialty of Hodogaya, which was one of the 53 Tokaido Stations. Another example is “Yosegizaiku” (which literally means “marquetry” in Japanese). It is a marquetry-like dessert combining a gelato flavored with Japanese cedar from Hakone with other gelatos flavored with spicebush, yabunikkei, and various other native trees of the Hakone mountains.

The beverage menu offers a selection of wines and local Japanese sake. There is also a list of alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks to pair with dishes. The menu is updated with new innovative drinks featuring local citrus fruits and wild plants. The modern, open dining room and kitchen are separated by a counter that seats 19. In addition, there are three private dining rooms. One of the walls is adorned with book paintings of food by an Italian-based Russian artist, Ekaterina Panikanova, to add color to the restaurant’s atmosphere.

Hakone Honbako, developed by Jiyujin, which is known for its project, Satoyama Jujo, in Niigata, shares the concept of local gastronomy with that sister project. This concept is also shared with Matsumoto Jujo’s Wood-fired grill restaurant, 367 (Sanrokunana), in Nagano. In principle, Hakone Honbako only accepts children of upper elementary age and older who can eat the same dishes as adults. Meanwhile, the restaurant offers commemorative plates for guests who want to celebrate important life events.

Come and dine at Hakone Honbako to delve into the heritage of Hakone and discover its food culture to satisfy your intellectual curiosity.

detail.longDescription: "Takumi Tatsuhiro" is an Edomae-style sushi restaurant located near Shinjuku Gyoen in Tokyo. Following the tradition of the famous sushi restaurant "Sushi Sho", customers can enjoy the unique style of enjoying side dishes in between sushi. Before opening his own sushi restaurant in August 2012, chef Tatsuhiro Nishi has gained a lot of experiences in Japanese restaurant in Kanazawa and several sushi restaurants in Tokyo, including "Sushisho" in Yotsuya. He not only gets his ingredients from Tsukiji, but also directly from Hokkaido, Kyushu, and Ishikawa. It is very important that the vineger rice balance with the seafood, the chef uses the "Hana Mizuki" rice from Ishikawa Prefecture, which is also his hometown. The chef visited the rice field, which is in a mountain that is surrounded by abundant nature, and talked with the producers before purchasing the rice. And for the sushi vinegar, the chef uses the blend of Fuji vinegar's red vinegar and rice vinegar from Kyoto's "Iio Jozo Vinegar Brewery". The vinegar brings out the flavor of the rice that matches with the seafood and creates a great combination. The chef serves the "omakase" course with the ten appetizers in between the 12 sushis, this tempo prevents customers from getting tired and full while satisfied with the course. There are ten seats at the main counter. The interior is decorated with beautiful polished wood which gives customers a comfortable environment. This restaurant is not only suitable for sushi dates and with a group of people, but also alone. There is a private room (up to 6 guests) where customers can use to bring important guests. From June 2017, one-minute walk from "Takumi Tatsuhiro", their other sushi restaurant "Sushi Band" is opened.

detail.longDescription:
Doing what you love to earn a livelihood. The owner-chef Shusaku Toba has pride in his calling and brings innovation to the Japanese restaurant industry as a spirited, energetic chef. After working at Italian restaurant ""DIRITTO"" in Kagurazaka and world gourmet guide award innovative restaurant ""Florilege"" in Azabudai, he took positions as sous chef at ""Tacubo"" in Daikanyama and chef at ""Gris"" in Yoyogiuehara before finally opening ""sio"" in the same place in 2018. The restaurant's name comes both from Japanese ""sio"" (salt) used in cooking as well as the acronym for ""Shuusaku Itsumo Oishii (Shusaku is always delicious),"" a most charming meaning. From this small, 16-seat restaurant arises a culinary reformation of a new age.

After his years rich with experience, Mr. Toba has arrived at the idea of a ""support-format committed restaurant."" By bringing together all the people who are involved in a restaurant—food producers, cutlery makers, interior designers, music creators—he aims to improve everyone's business and create a large movement. Mr. Toba has only one thought for ""sio"": to make unquestionably delicious food with his own hands and bring joy to his customers and other cooks. That's all. The chef's choice course is similar to ""Gris"" but more evolved, and while it is subtle and artistic, it focuses strongly on flavor and cheerfully transcends the boundaries of French cuisine with no regard for limits or genres.

Accompanying Mr. Toba's subtle cuisine are 6-7 types of tea pairings which do not hinder the food. Not concerned with providing the best match, the aim is simply to allow one to enjoy the variations of tea by providing tea pairings only to be found at ""sio,"" such as Taiwanese ""Tohobijin,"" blue tea, or carbonated jasmine tea. Wine is also offered, with 16 types including much natural French wine are available, and pairings are made just as with the teas. With his eloquence and diversity lending to his power as a chef, Mr. Toba's ""sio"" will pull forward the restaurant industry and become a flagship restaurant for reform.

detail.longDescription:
Udatsu Sushi, 5-minute walk from Nakameguro Station, a hidden sushi restaurant in the back alley. With the concept of "sushi restaurant in an art gallery," the space is decorated with pictures by famous artists from around the world. The sushi is made by Chef Hisashi Udatsu, who trained in sushi restaurants in Ginza and Nishiazabu.
 
It is based on traditional nigiri: one type of red vinegar and two types of rice vinegar, and one type of red vinegar and one type of rice vinegar. The rice used is Kinuhikari rice purchased from a contracted farmer in Tokyo. There is also Chef Udatsu's original nigiri sushi, the most recommended ones are "veggie roll" and "seasonal herb roll." "Veggie roll" is a sushi roll with several kinds of chopped seasonal vegetables. It is always served as one item when you change from side dishes to nigiri sushi, so you can start eating it refreshingly. "Seasonal herb roll" was developed when the chef was fascinated by the herbs when he visited "Kajitani Farm" in Mihara, Hiroshima. It is made by mixing microvegetables with ao-fish or white-meat fish purchased seasonally and wrapping it with nori.

"Smoked tuna" is popular as a side dish. A part of the tuna that has been skewered with a metal skewer and broiled with straw, then served in a glass container with a lid and sprinkled with truffle salt. The entertaining performance of putting smoke in the glass container and opening the lid in front of guests is also appreciated. The drink is supervised by Naotaka Ohashi, who is the former owner sommelier of TIRPSE and active as a food documenter. They have 6 to 10 types of sake, 2 types of white wine and 3 types of red wine, and 5 to10 types of champagne by the bottle.
 
There are 9 counter seats made of Yoshino cypress from Nara and a private room for 4 people. The paintings displayed in the chic mortared space change with the seasons. Enjoy a new style of sushi with your family, friends, couples, and colleagues.


*Awarded one star in the 2024 edition of the World Gourmet Guide Tokyo.

detail.longDescription:
A seven-minute walk from Temmabashi Station amidst the hustle and bustle of Osaka City, Sushi Hiramatsu is perched on the third floor of a building in Tsuriganecho, named after its symbol, a hanging bell cast as a tribute to Iemitsu, the third Shogun of the Tokugawa Shogunate (hanging bell is “tsurigane” in Japanese).  The restaurant is helmed by Chef Eikichi Hiramatsu, who worked many years at Sakagura Nakayama, a Japanese liquor store, where he amassed a knowledge of Japanese sake, and then trained and mastered the art of sushi at one of the most popular sushi restaurants in Osaka. He continued to work there as Branch Head Chef but eventually opened his own restaurant, Sushi Hiramatsu.  

The fish is sourced from carefully selected suppliers. For example, the common Edomae sushi toppings, such as bluefin tuna, bonito, and gizzard shad, are all transported by air from Toyosu Market, and the white fish for which the Akashi Strait is famous, such as sea bream, Japanese whiting, and squid, is purchased from a fishmonger’s shop in Kobe and turned into Edomae sushi toppings by the Kansai-born chef.  The sushi rice made of Yukiwakamaru, a premium brand rice from Yamagata, comes in three different flavors for different toppings. The white sushi rice for white fish with a mild acidity, a hint of salt, and a natural, sugar-free sweetness is matched up with delicately flavored white fish. The white sushi rice for gizzard shad is specially invented for gizzard shad but actually versatile and compatible with various other fishes, such as medium fatty bluefin tuna, prawn, horse mackerel, and bonito. The rosé sushi rice is mainly seasoned with red vinegar and salt to bring out the best flavors in the richly flavored toppings, such as blackthroat seaperch, sea urchin, conger eel, and clam.
 
The chef’s choice dinner features five small dishes and 10 pieces of nigiri sushi, followed by a Japanese-style omelet, soup, and desserts. Among them, the dry-aged bluefin tuna sushi, made of carefully selected bluefin tuna from Toyosu Market, is the chef’s signature dish, while the gizzard shad sushi, for which the gizzard shad is desalted at an incredibly slow pace, is the chef’s pride that tickles the taste buds of sushi lovers. The prawn sushi is also very popular for its rich flavor enhanced by boiling the prawns in a broth made from their shells. 

Sushi Hiramatsu offers an excellent selection of sake, curated by the chef based on his extensive experience and deep knowledge of sake. The restaurant always stores 20-odd varieties of sake, including Sohomare from Tochigi, Asahikiku from Fukuoka, Kakurei from Niigata, Koganesawa from Miyagi, Yamagata Masamune from Yamagata, Tenon from Shimane, and Kikuhime from Ishikawa, each served in glasses specially designed to unlock their flavors and aromas as intended by the chef. If you are not sure which sake to go with your food, you can ask the chef to choose for you.

Designed after a traditional Japanese-style house, the dining area is cozy with a comfortable counter (seating up to seven guests), as well as oil-filled electric heaters to keep the feet warm in winter.  The Osaka-style Edomae sushi crafted with heart and soul by Chef Hiramatsu makes any occasion unforgettable – whether it is personal or professional.
